items.stem: How did the teacher build up Bholi’s confidence on her first day at school?
items.answer: On the first day at school, Bholi was very frightened. When her teacher asked her name, she only stammered. At this, other children laughed at her, but her teacher motivated her to speak affectionately. At last she was able to speak her name to her teacher. Thus, the teacher built up Bholi’s confidence on her first day at school.

items.stem: Why was Ramlal worried about Bholi and not about his other children?
items.answer: Numberdar Ramlal was worried about his fourth child Bholi because her entire body was permanently disfigured by deep black pock- marks due to the attack of small pox. Secondly, she had neither good looks nor intelligence, and stammered from childhood due to her accident. Lastly, he was worried about her marriage because of her ugly face and lack of sense.

items.stem: When did Bholi begin to believe that she was going to a better place than her home? Or When did Bholi realize that she was going to a better place than her home?
items.answer: When Ramlal decide to send Bholi to school and asked her to come to school along with him, she was frightened because she did not know anything about school. She refused to go school. But, when she was dressed up properly with a clean dress, bathed and oiled her hair, she thought that she was going to a place better than her home.

items.stem: Why did Ramlal not send all his daughters to school?
items.answer: Ramlal had four daughters. Their names were Radha, Mangla, Champa and Bholi. The Tehsildar had asked Ramlal to send his daughters to school. Ramlal dared not disobey the Tehsildar. However, Ramlal did not send all his daughters to school because three of them were already married.

items.stem: In what respect was Bholi different from her sisters?
items.answer: Bholi was the weakest and youngest child of Ramlal. Bholi had ugly looks and absence of brain. Her sisters Radha, Mangla and Champa were healthy, strong and good looking. They had been happily married.

items.stem: Why were new and decent dresses given to Bholi when she started going to the school?
items.answer: Bholi was the youngest daughter of the revenue official Ramlal. He was worried about the reputation of his family in front of the teachers and other school girls, if Bholi was not sent to the school properly dressed. Because of this reason, Bholi was given dresses she had never worn before.

items.stem: How did Bholi’s teacher encourage her to speak without stammering?
items.answer: Bholi’s teacher encouraged her by trying to convince her that one day she would be the most learned one in the village, if she kept on studying. Then people would not laugh at her but listen to her with respect, at that time she would also be able to speak without the slightest stammer.

items.stem: Why were the relatives surprised when Bholi started speaking and refused to marry Bishamber?
items.answer: Bholi was not able to speak properly and had stammered since her childhood. But that day, she had spoken in a clear and loud voice asking Bishamber to return the five thousand rupees. Moreover, her courage in refusing to marry Bishamber for being greedy and humiliating her father, startled everybody.

items.stem: What did Bholi relate the pictures in the school wall to ?
items.answer: There were a lot of pictures on the school wall. Bholi related the picture of a horse with that of the Tehsildar’s horse, the picture of a goat with the goat in her neighbourhood, the picture of parrot she related to the parrots she had seen in the mango orchards and the cow looked like their cow Lakshmi.

items.stem: Imagine that Bholi wrties a diary entry, exploring the themes of ‘Girl Child’ and ‘Impact of Education’, in the context of her own experiences. Write this diary entry, as Bholi.
items.answer: February 20XX, Monday 9:00 pm Dear Diary, Today, I am feeling utmost proud of myself for rejecting the marriage with the old man (Bishamber Nath). From the moment I was born, I was ridiculed by my family members and friends because of my pock-marked face. People used to call me Bholi because they considered me a simpleton whom nobody would marry. My teacher showed me a world where my stammering voice and pockmarked face didn’t define me with her patience and kind words. Where others saw limitations, she saw potential in me. I’ve discovered my voice in education. I defied injustice today by declining to wed a man who treated me like a commodity. My education has given me the confidence to dream bigger and to challenge social norms. Bholi

items.stem: You and your friend have a conversation about prevalent discrimination between boys and girls, even today. Write the dialogue. You may begin like this: Friend: I don’t think discrimination in terms of gender is a thing of the past. You: ……………………………………… Friend: Hmmm. Yes, I agree, though we are in the 21st century it continues blatantly in many parts of the country. You: ………………………………….......
items.answer: Friend : I don’t think discrimination in terms of gender is a thing of the past. You : No, we are living in the 21st century where girls and boys are treated equally. Friend : Hmmm. Yes, I agree, though we are in the 21st century it still continues blatantly in many parts of the country. You : Exceptions are always there. Some states of India still face gender discrimination. I think our government is doing a lot to curb this practice. The 100% equality can be brought in only when the public participates. Friend : What can we do? You: We should educate our children and spread awareness among adults to stop discrimination among boys and girls. Friend: I think you are right.

items.stem: After reading Bholi’s story you decide to write a blog on the importance of educating the girl child and how it empowers her. Write that blog expressing your views.
items.answer: Power of Education Yesterday, I read the story of Bholi, a neglected child. It provoked me to rethink the importance of education; especially for a girl child. They say, “A teacher affects eternity, you never know how much the impact lasts”. Additionally, a mother is the first teacher of a child. If a mother is educated she can make a difference to the whole family’s thought process. Education broadens her intellect and awareness. Thus, she safeguards herself from dominating men in society. Bholi’s parents were marrying her off to a lame, greedy and middle- aged man. But, the power of education made her capable of raising her voice against it. Besides, she was confident enough to face the consequences of challenging the age-old stereotypes. Today, women can work in any field and earn money equal to their male counterparts. We must try to narrow the gap of gender discrimination by educating our girl children.

items.stem: Imagine you are Bholi and you have been invited by a girl’s secondary school in another village to address a group of students about being independent, fearless and breaking stereotypes. Write that speech.
items.answer: Hello students! It is an honour to stand here and share my life experiences with you. Today, you find me a confident and self-dependent girl. But it was totally opposite before I joined a school. I was fearful, dependent, ignorant and a stammerer. But, my school helped me to get educated and my teacher supported me in bringing out my hidden confidence. Education is a weapon. You get a chance to explore your latent talents and capabilities through education which makes you fearless. A confident person can distinguish between right and wrong. You must think twice before accepting the stereotypes laid down by society for us. Through education, I could muster up the courage to refuse to marry a greedy man who disgraced my parents. Today, I can earn like my brother and give financial support to my old parents. In the end, I want to say that you must educate yourself and show your real worth to the world. Good Luck to all of you!

items.stem: What do you know about Bishamber Nath? Why did Bholi refuse to marry him?
items.answer: Bishambar Nath was a middle aged man. He was a well-to-do grocer and lived in another village. He was a widower and had children from his first wife. He was of the same age as Bholi’s father and was a rich man. He owned a house, a shop and much money in the bank. When he showed his willingness to marry Bholi, her parents were more than happy that she would get married to someone who was not asking for any dowry. Bholi too agreed to the match at first to fulfil her parents wishes. Later on, she rejected the marriage when the bridegroom asked for dowry. This tells us that Bholi was not a timid and dumb girl. She was aware of her rights. She also knew how to fight for her own dignity and feared no-one. She had become confident and bold after being educated. So she refused to marry a lame, old, greedy man, Bishambar Nath.

items.stem: ‘Don’t you worry, Pitaji! In your old age I will serve you and mother.’ Through this statement the narrator wants to highlight the moral values Bholi was imbued with. Based on the reading of the lesson, what made Bholi aware of her rights and how did she use them?
items.answer: ‘Don’t you worry, Pitaji! In your old age I will serve you and mother.’ Through this bold statement of Bholi (now Sulekha), we understand her sense of responsibility, courage and confidence in life. It is the teacher of her school who inculcated a sense of responsibility in Bholi and taught her how to lead a respectable life. She made her aware of her rights in the society in order to change social norms. Bholi is the narrator’s voice in story that represents the drama of her life. Once she was a simpleton - a dumb cow, now a responsible, fearless and intelligent woman to perform her basic rights. In the context, Bholi refused to marry greedy Bishamber, and proved the woman’s rights, assuring her parents that she would shoulder their responsibility.

items.stem: Bholi was believed to be a ‘dumb cow’. What turned her into a fearless, bold and confident girl?
items.answer: There is no doubt that Bholi was believed to be a ‘dumb cow’. Everybody used to call her Bholi, the simpleton, because she stammered. But, the teacher’s love, inspiration and affection impressed her a lot. The teacher taught her how to lead a respectable life. She motivated her to be the most educated person in the village. So, Bholi got a new hope and a new life at school. It is her teacher who changed her life and brought a sea change in her personality. In the end of the story we see that Bholi’s refusal to marry greedy Bishamber proved that she was courageous enough and could distinguish between right and wrong. Thus, it is her education and the teacher’s help that turned her into a fearless, bold and confident girl.

items.stem: The story, ‘Bholi’ throws light on some social evils being practised in our society. Bholi took a stand and succeeded in overcoming social barriers. What can you contribute to change the social attitudes illustrated in the story?
items.answer: In our society, we find that social evils are being practised due to illiteracy and ignorance. In the story, we see that Bholi is a classic example of how the social evils deprived her of getting equal opportunities. The social attitudes, particularly in Indian villages, are making the girls underprivileged and discriminated against to get their rights in the society. In the story, we see that Bholi’s teacher helped her overcome social barriers by encouraging and motivating her to understand her rights in the society. Bholi took a stand and succeed in overcoming social barriers, challenging the age- old superstitions - dowry and child marriage. We can challenge these social barriers like dowry and male domination by empowering the women through spreading the light of education among them. We can contribute towards changing the social attitudes illustrated in the story by educating the people, especially girls because education makes them self-confident, courageous, responsible and intelligent.

items.stem: On the basis of your understanding of the story, sketch the character of Bholi and describe the role the teacher played in her life. Or Bholi was known to be “dumb cow”. How did she turn out to be an outspoken and fearless girl ? Or On the basis of your understanding of the story, sketch the character of Bholi.
items.answer: Bholi was a simpleton. She lacked sense, her body was disfigured with the pockmarks and she looked ugly. Moreover, she stammered while speaking. That is why, she was ignored and was often laughed at. Therefore, she suffered from inferiority complex and felt ashamed of herself. But with the encouragement and affection of her teacher, her entire life changed for the better. It was her education which moulded her into a bold and courageous girl. She could now take her own decisions and could not be cowed down by anyone. She refused to marry the man, who humiliated her father. On top of that, she did not stammer anymore and spoke clearly. It was all due to the role her teacher played in her life, which transformed her into a girl who was bold enough to take independent decisions. At the end, she was determined to be a teacher in the school from where she had gained a lot.

items.chapter: The Book That Saved The Earth
items.stem: How does Think-Tank react after seeing the picture of Humpty Dumpty in the book ‘Mother Goose’ ?
items.answer: After seeing the picture of Humpty Dumpty in book ‘Mother Goose’, Think-Tank screamed, and holding his head, he said that the picture was of him and his Great and Mighty Balloon Brain. He further explained that the Earthlings had seen him and were now after him.

items.chapter: The Book That Saved The Earth
items.stem: Why did Think-Tank react in alarm to the third passage to read?
items.answer: Think-Tank reacted in alarm as he misunderstood the meaning of the poem and thought that they could actually grow crops of rare metals and even explosives also, which were dangerous for him.

items.chapter: The Book That Saved The Earth
items.stem: Why did Think-Tank send his crew on the earth?
items.answer: Think-Tank, the ruler of Mars regarded the earth as a mass of mud, and Earthlings as ugly, tiny-headed creatures. He planned to invade the earth and expand his domain. He sent Probe One to Earth to get more information about the Earthlings.

items.chapter: The Book That Saved The Earth
items.stem: How does Think-Tank describe the people on the earth? Why does he command Noodle to contact the Space probe?
items.answer: Think-Tank thought Earthlings were weak, ignorant, uncivilized persons and hence planned to invade the earth. He sent his commander Noodle to make contact with the crew of the manned space probe, now on Earth to seek more information about the Earth.

items.chapter: The Book That Saved The Earth
items.stem: Who was Omega? Why did he try to eat the book?
items.answer: Omega was the captain of the space control Probe One, on the earth. Think-Tank asked him to pick up the most colourful sandwich (book) and report him about his observation on it.

items.chapter: The Book That Saved The Earth
items.stem: Why books referred to as a man’s best companion? Which book saved the Earth from Martian invasion?
items.answer: Books are our best friends and companions. They are never demanding but always giving knowledge and pleasure. They give us company. The book that saved the Earth from Martian invasion was ‘Mother Goose.’

items.chapter: The Book That Saved The Earth
items.stem: How did Apprentice Noodle act smartly by suggesting something about the book without offending Think-Tank ?
items.answer: In “The Book That Saved the Earth,” Apprentice Noodle acts smartly by suggesting that the book, initially misunderstood as a “sandwich” by Think- Tank, might be a communication device-specifically, a “corn communicator” due to its resemblance to corn, which they speculate could be Earth’s primary form of communication. This suggestion cleverly shifts Think-Tank’s perception of the book without directly contradicting or offending him, preserving his ego. Noodle’s tactful approach allows Think-Tank to reconsider his stance without feeling challenged, showcasing Noodle’s ability to navigate the delicate situation wisely. This move not only prevents direct confrontation but also plays a crucial role in the unfolding events, highlighting how diplomacy and creative thinking can influence outcomes positively

items.chapter: The Book That Saved The Earth
items.stem: It is morally incorrect to invade another country/ planet for one’s own benefit. The Martians did not understand the value of peaceful coexistence. How did the book of nursery rhymes save the Earth from the Martian invasion?
items.answer: Great and Mighty Think-Tank believed that the Martians were a superior race so they must invade and put the Earth under his generous rulership. He scornfully called the Earth ‘primitive ball of mud’. The Martians did not understand the value of peaceful co-existence and sent a mission to invade the Earth. The crew landed in a library and could not make out what the books were actually. It was believed that the books were a sort of communication device. Think-Tank asked the members to decipher the code of the ‘sandwiches’. The nursery rhymes were totally misinterpreted and it was believed that the Earthlings had developed an advance civilization and were planning to invade the Mars. The mission was called off and the Martians escaped to a remote place to save their lives. Thus the books saved the Earth.

items.chapter: The Book That Saved The Earth
items.stem: What guesses are made by Think-Tank about the books found on Earth? Or What does Noodle tell Think-Tank about the book? Or Noodle avoids offending Think-Tank but at the same time he corrects his mistakes. How does he manage to do that?
items.answer: Think-Tank at first thinks the book found on Earth was a sandwich. His next opinion was that they were actually communication sandwiches which were meant for ear communication. Later, on Noodle’s suggestion, he agrees that the book is meant for eye communication. Noodle asks Think- Tank to observe these so-called ‘sandwiches’ by consuming certain vitamins given to the space people by the chemical department to increase their intelligence. The meaning of the code would then slowly unfold before them. In this way Noodle manages to correct him without offending him.

items.chapter: The Book That Saved The Earth
items.stem: How do the three nursery rhymes frighten Think- Tank in the story, ‘The Book That Saved the Earth’?
items.answer: The rhyme ‘Mistress Mary, quite contrary’ makes Think-Tank believe that the Earthlings have discovered how to combine agriculture and mining. He thinks that they can grow explosives. The rhyme ‘Hey diddle diddle!’ makes him conclude that the Earthlings have reached a high level of civilization; even their animals have musical culture and know space techniques. He fears that at that very moment, the Earthlings might be launching an interplanetary attack of millions of cows. Oop reads the rhyme ‘Humpty Dumpty’ and shows him a picture of Humpty Dumpty. Think-Tank concludes that it is his picture and the Earthlings are planning to invade Mars.

items.chapter: The Book That Saved The Earth
items.stem: Attempt character sketch of Great and Mighty Think-Tank.
items.answer: Great and Mighty Think-Tank is introduced to us to be the most mighty, powerful and intelligent creature. He is regarded as the ruler of Mars who is very proud of being Martian. His pride makes him consult mirror to hear self-praise. He has a quick mind and wishes to attack the Earth in a great hurry. The ways he makes guesses about the book are also funny. He has respect for no one in front of him and regards others views as trifling. But still his wit is too great. He makes Omega swallow. the vitamin to decipher the code. At every nursery rhyme, he prepares to go to Earth for invasion. He is also fickle-minded. One moment he orders the invasion to be taken next day and then he orders for immediate invasion. He ordered the invasion flat to evacuate the entire planet and head for Alpha Centauri. It is his commanding power which earns him name of general.

items.chapter: The Book That Saved The Earth
items.stem: Justify the title of the play ‘The Book that Saved the Earth’.
items.answer: A good title should reflect the theme, idea or the traits of a character. It should revolve around any of the above. The story or the play should be woven around any one of them. In the play ‘The Book that Saved The Earth’, a book of nurse rhymes of ‘Mother Goose’ is responsible for stopping the Martian invasion on Earth. Think-Tank, the ruler of Mars plans to invade Earth before lunch and sends Probe One to get more information about the Earthlings. They enter a library but can’t figure out what items books are. They take vitamins, increase their intelligence then read the rhymes from ‘Mother Goose’. Think-Tank misinterprets the rhymes, takes them as threats to him and the Mars. Scared, he calls back Probe One, drops the idea of invading and escapes with his subjects to Alpha Centauri, a hundred million miles away from Mars. Thus, the book ‘Mother Goose’ was responsible for stopping the Martian invasion of Earth. The title ‘The Book That Saved the Earth’, reflect the theme of the play, so it is an apt (appropriate) title.

items.chapter: The Book That Saved The Earth
items.stem: How was the crew of Space Probe One able to describe the code of the book ‘Mother Goose’ ?
items.answer: Think-Tank had asked Captain Omega to take the large, colourful ‘sandwich’ he had pointed at and tell him what was observed by her. The book Omega had picked up was a very large volume of ‘Mother Goose’, a book of nursery rhymes, which Think-Tank thought was a sandwich. Captain Omega had said that the book appeared to contain pictures of the Earthlings. Iota had said that there seemed to be some sort of code written in the book as well. Think-Tank had then asked Sergeant Oop to describe the code, and he had told him that there were little lines and squiggles and dots- thousands of those codes alongside the pictures. At that moment, Noodle had politely pointed out that their chemical department people had given the space people vitamins to increase their intelligence. Saying that he had a thought of magnificent brilliance, Think-Tank then asked Omega and the others to take the vitamins immediately. They swallowed those vitamins and therefore were able to describe the code.

items.chapter: The Book That Saved The Earth
items.stem: What does Think-Tank say the Earthlings can grow ? How does he react to it ?
items.answer: Think-Tank misinterpreted the lines of the nursery rhyme : Mistress Mary, quite coutrary, How does your garden grow ? With cockle shells and silvers bells, And pretty maids all in a row. Oops commented jokingly that pretty maids were growing in a garden. But Think-Tank asked him to stop his foolishness. Alarmingly, Think-Tank commented that the Earthlings had discovered how to combine agriculture and mining. He said that the Earthlings could actually grow crops of rare metals such as silver, cockle shells and even grow high explosives. Think-Tank had then told Noodle to contact their invasion fleet immediately and to tell them to hold the invasion because he had realised that he should not underestimate the Earthlings.

items.chapter: The Book That Saved The Earth
items.stem: ‘Pride has a fall’. Justify this statement giving relevant points from how Think-Tank reacted to the readings from Mother Goose.
items.answer: Martians invaded the earth and reached in a library. Think-Tank was their boss. He was very proud of his wisdom, as he was having a big balloon like head. He thought that he was the wisest person on Mars. Nobody could disobey him, or even dare to speak against him. He claimed that he had a quick mind. He had no respect for anyone and regarded other’s views as trifling. He was also fickle-minded. He misinterpreted the rhymes in a complete verbal manner. The rhyme mistress Mar made him ponder over the discovery of the earth. From the poem diddle-diddle he got alarmed and from the poem Humpty-Dumpty, he was so frightened that he decided to leave his kingdom and run away to Alpha Centauri. Thus his great wisdom was defeated and had a great fall.

items.chapter: The Book That Saved The Earth
items.stem: Attempt a character-sketch of Noodle highlighting the values projected by him.
items.answer: Noodle is one of the crew members of the invasion team that came to invade earth. He is known as Apprentice Noodle. He is the co-coordinator between Think-Tank and the invasion team. He echoes Think-Tank in every manner. He is a very clever creature. He knows that Think-Tank being the commander-in-chief has to be obeyed. So he keeps on praising Think-Tank and also passing sarcastic remarks. It is only Noodles who think practically and differently about the books which were considered as sandwiches to eat. But Think- Tank took over the idea as his own. But Noodle is not sad at all. He is a blind and true follower of Think-Tank.

items.chapter: The Book That Saved The Earth
items.stem: Read the extract given below and answer the questions that follows : Omega : Listen to them? Iota and Oop: (To each other, puzzled): Listen to them? Think-Tank: Do you have marbles in your ears? I said, listen to them. (Martians bow very low). Omega: It shall be done, sir. (They each take two books from the case and hold them to their ears, listening intently.) Iota : (whispering to Omega) Do you hear anything? Omega : (Whispering back) Nothing. Do you hear anything, Oop? Oop : (Loudly) Not a thing! (Omega and Iota jump in fright.) Omega and Iota : Sh-h-h! (They listen intently again). Think-Tank : Well? Well? Report to me. What do you hear? Omega : Nothing, sir. Perhaps we are not on the correct frequency. Iota : Nothing, sir. Perhaps the Earthlings have sharper ears than we do. Oop : I don’t hear a thing. Maybe these sandwiches don’t make sounds. i. Where are Omega, Oop and Iota in this conversation? ii. How does Think-Tank explain the books to his probe crew? iii. Describe Think-Tank in your our words. iv. Who made the next guess about what the sandwiches actually were? What was the guess?
items.answer: i. Omega, Oop and Iota are at the Centerville Public Library. ii. Think-Tank told his crew that the books were communication devices and asked the probe crew to listen to them. iii. Think-Tank was the ruler of the planet Mars. His head is huge and egg-shaped. He wears a robe decorated with stars and circles. He considered himself very mighty and was very proud of his intelligence. iv. Noodle made the next guess about what the sandwiches actually were. He guessed that the sandwiches were something to be watched. 
